title: nLight Wired Product Primer
summary: An introduction to the nLight Wired networked lighting control platform: topology, cabling, and where it fits.

blocks.content: nLight Wired is a digital, networked lighting control platform. Devices (sensors, wall pods, power/relay packs) connect over standard CAT-5e cabling and communicate on a device network.
Because it is networked and addressable, nLight supports grouping, scheduling, and data — not just standalone room control.
nLight devices are daisy-chained or connected in a free topology using CAT-5e patch cables. A bridge connects device groups to the larger network and to SensorView for management.
CAT-5e carries both low-voltage power and data between many nLight devices — respect device-count and cable-length limits per zone/bridge.
Choose nLight Wired for new construction or renovations where running low-voltage cable is practical and the owner wants networked control, scheduling, and reporting.
When pulling cable is impractical (retrofits, historic buildings), consider a wireless platform such as nLight Air instead.

questions.prompt: What cabling does nLight Wired primarily use between devices?
questions.explanation: nLight Wired devices connect over standard CAT-5e patch cabling.

questions.prompt: What device connects nLight device groups to the wider network and SensorView?
questions.explanation: A bridge links device groups to the larger network and to SensorView management.

questions.prompt: True or False: nLight Wired is addressable and networked, supporting grouping, scheduling, and data.
questions.explanation: Being networked and addressable is exactly what distinguishes nLight from standalone room control.

questions.prompt: When is nLight Air (wireless) often a better fit than nLight Wired?

choices.text: When running low-voltage cable is impractical (retrofits, historic buildings)
When the owner wants no controls at all

questions.explanation: Wireless nLight Air shines where pulling cable is impractical, such as retrofits.
